reuse.why: All bulk actions use the existing category selector, and the new action reuses the existing amount-sign, sheet-access, budget-write, batching and undo abstractions.

duplication.why: Category eligibility and amount-sign decisions remain shared, with no substantive duplicated decision logic introduced.

placement.why: Eligibility and budget calculations remain in budget/actions.ts, while method registration and undo wrapping follow the existing app.ts pattern.

scope.why: The edits address the requested bulk actions, although adding goal_def to getBudgetData is unnecessary because eligibility is determined by the shared selector.

maintainability.why: The shared selector keeps evolving exclusions consistent across consumers, with only minor cleanup needed around the unused query field and repeated argument types.

bypasses_abstraction.where: Every changed month-wide action, including setLastMonthSpending, routes category eligibility through getBulkBudgetCategories.

disguised_duplication.where: The new action shares eligibility and sign conversion rather than reshaping copies of those decisions.

abstraction_drift.where: getBulkBudgetCategories replaces its existing includeHidden parameter with includeHiddenCategories and adds shared template and fixed-group exclusion branches; no consumer-specific branches or bypasses are introduced.
